$comment: Shared engine-neutral case table for the openapi family specifications §§9.2–9.3. Each whole-document cell crosses edition, form media, resolved property kind, Schema content keyword, and Encoding contentType. Corrected 2026-08-26: typeless multipart cells no longer carry the superseded refusal. On 3.1 they use the raw-octet lane and canonical Base64 boundary, defaulting to application/octet-stream when Encoding contentType is absent. On 3.0 they remain represented but require configuration.propertyMedia at invocation; this harness supplies none, so they decide missing-required-choice. Typeless urlencoded cells remain refused because the family defines no urlencoded raw-octet boundary. contentEncoding is inert off string, and 3.1 emits no Content-Transfer-Encoding.

bases.r4-urlencoded-array-container: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01). The property declares type: array with string items and rides the content-based urlencoded lane, where the WHOLE array is one field value. The accepted editions derive an array's default contentType from its ITEMS -- here a plain string, so text/plain -- and no accepted edition states what an array looks like under text/plain. The engines previously returned application/json for any array, reading the default off the CONTAINER and authoring bytes no edition selected. R4 keeps the item-derived default exactly as the editions state it and gives the ungoverned container cell the remedy the family documents' section 9.3 configuration point already carries: one concrete `propertyMedia` choice, absent which the invocation refuses before dispatch as the context-required species. This table supplies no choice, so these cells decide missing-required-choice. Every `contentEncoding` and `contentMediaType` spelling lands on the same answer as its |plain twin, because the cell is decided by the container's missing serialization and not by an annotation on the item. An explicit Encoding contentType (encCT present) is unaffected: the artifact made the choice, so no configuration is required.
